intro: This AI video generator turns a photo, a product page link or a short description into a clip, without filming, actors on set or a production crew. Every clip is centered on your product.

Choose a creator-style ad, a demo, an unboxing or a visible change, then set a 9:16, 1:1 or 16:9 frame and a length of 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds. Each run makes one clip, and the credit cost appears before you start.

faq.q: How do I make an AI video from a product photo?
faq.a: Upload one clear photo of your item or paste a product page link, choose a video type, frame and length, and run the job. The tool builds the clip around your product and shows the credit cost before you start.

faq.q: How long and wide can an AI video be?
faq.a: You can choose 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds, with 9:16 vertical, 1:1 square and 16:9 wide frames. There are also 3:4 and 4:3 options for listings and pages.
The price shows before each run. A 6-second clip uses 24 credits, 10 seconds uses 40, 15 seconds uses 60 and half a minute uses 120. If a job fails, the credits return automatically.

faq.q: Can I make several versions for A/B testing?
faq.a: Yes. Run the same photo with different actors, openings or scenes, then split-test the downloads in your ad platform without booking another shoot.

faq.q: Can I enter a product page URL instead of a photo?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the link into URL to Video and the tool brings the product image and name into the editor for you to check before making the clip.

faq.q: Do I need to hire a model or creator?
faq.a: No. The people in the clips are generated around your product photo, so there is no casting, sample shipping or filming date. You can still work with a real creator later.

faq.q: Are these clips suitable for paid social ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloads are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube. Add your own captions, prices and offers and follow each platform's AI labeling rules.

faq.q: How long does a video take to make?
faq.a: A finished clip is ready in minutes, and the exact time varies with the length and server load. You can start another job while you wait.
